tagline: Three miles of Gulf Drive, with the beach right alongside.
intro: Over the drawbridge at Longboat Pass, Gulf Drive comes onto Anna Maria Island and runs north through Bradenton Beach, the Gulf of Mexico immediately to the west and Anna Maria Sound to the east. The scenic highway is about three miles of it, to the north city limits, laid out for walking and biking, with beaches, picnic spots and boat ramps along the way.
The town was Cortez Beach until the land boom of the 1920s, when developers decided a name that sounded closer to Bradenton would sell better. Its bridges have had a rough time of it.

moments.title: Longboat Pass
moments.text: The first wooden bridge to Longboat Key opened in August 1926, was damaged by a hurricane that October and swept away in 1932, and nothing replaced it until 1957.

moments.title: Bradenton Beach
moments.text: When a concrete bridge from Cortez replaced the wooden one in 1957, the town showed residents how strong it was with a parade led by an elephant.

moments.title: Wreck of the Regina
moments.text: Just offshore lies the Belfast-built tanker barge that went down on a sandbar in March 1940 with a cargo of molasses, now one of Florida's underwater archaeological preserves.
